1000.title: THelpViewer
content: [b]THelpViewer context-sensitive help[/b]
Press F1 anywhere to open the topic assigned to the active view.
Links, long topics and fixed-width tables use the same UHF 2.0 data
model as converted DOS HELP files.
│ Key              │ Action                                     │
│ F1               │ Context help                               │
│ F10              │ Activate the menu bar                      │
│ F5               │ Zoom or restore the active window          │
│ F6 / Shift-F6    │ Select next or previous window             │
│ Alt-F3           │ Close the active window                    │
[link:topic=2090]Clipboard[/link]: Ctrl+Ins copies, Shift+Del cuts, Shift+Ins pastes.
Use Cmd+C/X/V on macOS or Ctrl+C/X/V on Windows/Linux too.
Topics:
[link:topic=1200]HELP files[/link]   [link:topic=1300]Documents[/link]   [link:topic=1400]Search[/link]
[link:topic=1500]Games[/link]        [link:topic=1600]Windows[/link]     [link:topic=2090]Dialogs[/link]
[link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]   [link:topic=2060]MIDI Player[/link]  [link:topic=2280]Account[/link]
The status line and Help menu invoke this same help file. Each
TVView or managed window supplies a Turbo Vision-style helpCtx.
Use Help > Index to browse the alphabetical topic index.
This intentionally contains enough text to exercise the shared
vertical scrollbar. Future application documentation can be added as
ordinary UHF topics without changing the JavaScript window.
[link:topic=1700]How context help is resolved[/link]

1100.title: System menu
content: The system menu contains utilities, palette editing, Widget Gallery,
System Information, screen savers and theme selection. About is in
the Help menu.
See also: [link:topic=2040]Colors[/link]  [link:topic=2270]System Information[/link]
[link:topic=2050]Widget Gallery[/link]  [link:topic=2130]Screen saver[/link]

1200.title: HELP files
content: Open installs a HELP or Docs file from the generated catalog.
Catalog submenus open a source directly.
Cross-file links retain the real source filename and open the target
when its bundle exists in the catalog.
See also: [link:topic=2010]Open a File[/link]  [link:topic=2070]HELP viewer[/link]

1300.title: Documents
content: Markdown documentation opens in a read-only Editor-style window with
a blue background and yellow base text.
Use Ctrl-F to find text and Ctrl-L to repeat the search.
See also: [link:topic=2030]Find[/link]  [link:topic=2080]Document viewer[/link]

1400.title: Search
content: Choose Search all HELP/Docs for server-wide full-text/topic search,
or Find in active window for local HELP/Docs text. Only available
scopes are enabled. Find Again repeats the active window's query.
Search Topics lists matching topics with source information; the
line below the list shows the original HELP's long title.
The server builds a persistent index when sources change. Its
progress dialog can be hidden without stopping indexing.
Completed data stays available during updates. Unreadable files are
reported as skipped; other files remain searchable. Fix the source
and the server retries it after its content or permissions change.
See also: [link:topic=2030]Find dialog[/link]

1500.title: Games
content: Games share Turbo Vision dialogs, keyboard focus, inactive-window
pause policies and a shared server ten-entry Hall of Fame.
The [H] title control opens scores. Its brackets use the title color
and H uses the common frame-icon color.

1600.title: Windows
content: Tile, Cascade and Window List arrange managed windows.
F5 zooms, F6 selects the next window and Alt-F3 closes the active
target. Window controls use the shared TVFrame/TVWindow rendering.

1700.title: Context Help
content: The active menu item has first priority, followed by the focused view,
the active managed dialog/window and finally the application context.
The resolved hc... number selects a topic in THELPVIEWER.HLP, stored
as a UHF 2.0 JSON bundle.
[link:topic=1000]Return to Help Contents[/link]

2000.title: About
content: About shows the application version and authors. The version comes
from the running package metadata rather than a hard-coded string.

2010.title: Open a File
content: Choose a HELP or Docs file from the two-column list.
The ▐↓▌ control opens recent files. The History window has its own
close control, and also closes with Escape or a click outside.
Enter opens the selected file. Double-clicking a directory enters it.
See also: [link:topic=2020]Change Directory[/link]  [link:topic=1200]HELP files[/link]

2020.title: Change Directory
content: Select a virtual HELP/DOCS directory. Chdir applies it to Open a File;
Revert restores the initial path. The History control uses the same
TVHistoryWindow implementation as Open a File and Find.

2030.title: Find
content: Choose one scope: Search all HELP/Docs or Find in active window.
The first input is focused so you can type immediately. Alt-F uses
the Find label to focus its linked input. The arrow opens query
history; Escape, the arrow again or its close control dismisses it.
Find Again repeats the active window's current query.
[link:topic=1400]Search and global index[/link]

2040.title: Colors
content: Choose a Group and Item, then edit its DOS foreground/background
attribute. Default restores the selected item. Reset All restores the
complete Turbo Vision palette.
All users may edit colors, not only administrators. Open Colors from
your user menu > Configuration (guests use the system menu). Saved in
this browser, not synchronized between accounts or devices.

2050.title: Widget Gallery
content: Widget Gallery exercises shared labels, inputs, list viewers, list
boxes, clusters, scrollbars, buttons, static text, terminal, outline
and message-box components.

2060.title: CD/MIDI Player
content: Play game MIDI music with the SoundFont synthesizer. The cover is
shown when the configured source supplies one. Play, Pause and Stop
control playback; clicking the progress bar seeks within the song.
More reveals the track list, Filter with history and Random next
track. A finished song starts the next one in order or at random.
Administrators choose providers in [link:topic=2315]Configuration > MIDI Sources[/link].
A cloud symbol at the row's end marks a track not downloaded yet.
Playing it prioritizes its download; background downloading resumes
afterwards. The requested track goes to the front of the shared queue
and can download during a HELP/DOS transfer. Repeated requests do not
start duplicate transfers. [link:topic=2316]Downloads[/link] beside the clock shows progress.
Open that menu for the shared package and MIDI album queue.
It does not create an additional automatic MIDI progress window.
Closing the menu does not stop downloading. ZIP track totals may grow
after extracting their members.
RIFF/RMID and counted DOS MIDI are decoded to playable Standard MIDI.
A partial library shows ready tracks and the download-error count.
See Downloads for the failed album/member; other music remains usable.
The server caches tracks, covers and the catalog under var/midi.
Playback statistics count plays and actual time, excluding pauses.
Local admins may rebuild this library from midi-sources.json.
[link:topic=2310]Server Configuration and Rebuild[/link]

2070.title: HELP viewer
content: Links open topics or companion HELP files. Use Back, Index, Contents
and Search from the status line or menus. The viewer renders UHF 2.0
links, styles, fixed-width text and source-defined colors.
Native TextScreens keep original glyphs and palette colors with
embedded fonts; they share this window and its scrollbars.
Native blink attributes are retained; reduced motion keeps them visible.
Native aliases open their real topic. If a link has no destination,
Help Error explains the failure and the current page stays open.
Previous and Next follow the active topic's defined continuation.
They appear only when another page exists, not for hotspot selection.
A file without an index opens its available Contents before a topic.
In multi-page Sidekick help, click More.. to continue or use Content
to select Page 2, Page 3 and later pages directly.

2080.title: Document viewer
content: Markdown is displayed through the read-only Editor palette. The lower
left indicator reports RO plus the current line and column.
Select text and press Ctrl+Ins or your system's Copy shortcut.
Cut and Paste cannot change this read-only document.

2090.title: Dialogs
content: Tab and Shift-Tab move focus. Enter activates the default button and
Escape closes the dialog unless its active control reserves Escape.
Clicking outside a dialog never closes it; modal dialogs block input.
[b]System clipboard[/b]
Copy: Ctrl+Ins. Cut: Shift+Del. Paste: Shift+Ins.
macOS: Cmd+C/X/V. Windows/Linux: Ctrl+C/X/V.
These work in shared input fields; Paste respects format and length.
Selected HELP/Docs text can be copied but cannot be cut or replaced.
Browser permissions may limit clipboard access. Use native shortcuts
or the browser menu if requested. Clipboard text is never sent to
the server or saved in application data.
Common dialogs:
[link:topic=2010]Open a File[/link]       [link:topic=2020]Change Directory[/link]
[link:topic=2030]Find[/link]              [link:topic=2040]Colors[/link]
[link:topic=2050]Widget Gallery[/link]    [link:topic=2060]CD/MIDI Player[/link]

2100.title: Calendar
content: Browse months and years with the arrow controls. Date calculations use
Gregorian leap-year rules.

2110.title: ASCII Table
content: Shows character codes and glyphs using the configured DOS code-page
presentation.

2120.title: Calculator
content: Use number and operation buttons or the keyboard. Escape is reserved
by the calculator and does not close it.

2130.title: Screen saver
content: Choose a mode from the system menu. Input stops the saver and restores
the previously focused control.

2140.title: Puzzle
content: Move a tile next to the blank square with the mouse or arrow keys.
Solve the shuffled 4 x 4 board in as few moves as possible.
The [H] title control opens the Puzzle Hall of Fame.

2150.title: Tetris
content: New starts a game. Left and Right move the piece, Up rotates it and
Down drops it faster. P pauses the timer. Pentix toggles the extended
piece set.
The game pauses whenever its window is inactive.

2160.title: Mines
content: Reveal safe squares and mark suspected mines. A revealed number tells
how many mines touch that square.
The timer pauses whenever the Mines window is inactive.

2170.title: BreakOut
content: Move the paddle, keep the ball in play and clear all bricks.
Keyboard and pointer controls share the same game state.
The animation pauses whenever the window is inactive.

2180.title: Sokoban
content: Push every crate onto a goal. Arrow keys move the player.
Crates can be pushed but cannot be pulled, so plan each move.
After solving a level, press Enter for the next one. On leaving
the game, Hall of Fame ranks the level reached first, then moves.

2190.title: Lines
content: Select a coloured ball and move it along a free path. Build lines to
score and remove balls before the board fills.

2200.title: Reversi
content: Place a disc that brackets one or more opposing discs. Bracketed discs
change colour. The player with the most discs at the end wins.

2210.title: Ludo
content: Roll the die and choose a legal piece. Move every piece around the
board and into home before the other players.

2220.title: Mastermind
content: Build a colour guess and submit it. Feedback reports colours in the
correct position separately from correct colours in other positions.

2230.title: Snake
content: Use the arrow keys to steer. Eat food to grow without hitting the wall
or your own body. The game pauses while its window is inactive.

2240.title: Tower of Hanoi
content: Move the complete stack to another peg without placing a larger disc
on a smaller one. Use pointer or keyboard controls; the move history
records every completed move.

2250.title: Tron Light Cycles
content: Steer both cycles simultaneously and avoid walls and every light trail.
The timer and movement pause whenever the game window is inactive.

2260.title: Server Statistics
content: A Turbo Vision dialog shows visits, opened content, search/link outcomes,
games, environment and coarse performance intervals. It also shows active
viewing intervals for HELP files, documents, dialogs and games.
DOS Prompt opens/time and per-track MIDI plays/listening time are
included. MIDI listening time excludes paused playback.
Target time pauses while another window or browser tab is active.
SQLite stores aggregate counters only. It does not store IP addresses,
cookies, visitor IDs, search text, exact timings, full referrers, raw user
agents or individual visits.

2270.title: System Information
content: This dialog shows local application, browser, display, locale, storage
and web-capability information. Its Server section reports server
status, application version and HELP/Docs catalog sizes.
Refresh measures the current runtime again. Opening this dialog does
not submit the displayed details to visitor statistics.

2280.title: Account and Login
content: Login appears at the right of the menu bar. After sign-in it becomes
your display name, with Account, Configuration and Sign Out.
Account edits first/last name, nickname and email.
The menu uses nickname, then first/last name; no Display name field.
If personal fields are blank, the existing account label is retained.
Email is validated before Save. Save updates the menu and closes
the dialog. Cancel/close does not save. Role is shown, not editable.
Private C shows saved overlay usage and capacity (excluding common games).
Profile Save preserves username, Passkeys, sessions and private DOS files.
Account also lists your named Passkeys. Select one, edit its name and
press Rename, or enter a name and Add Passkey for another authenticator.
Registration suggests an editable OS/browser name, not device identity.
Synchronized keys may work on several devices. Old keys can be renamed.
Set an optional password by entering it twice (15-128 characters).
Alt+P focuses New password.
Use a long, unique passphrase; basic predictable values are rejected.
Setting a password or adding a key asks for existing Passkey confirmation.
Security actions save immediately, independently of profile Save/Cancel.
Changing a password signs out other sessions, not your current session.
The new email or original username works for login; email is unverified.
Enter your email or legacy username, press Sign In and approve the
Passkey prompt, or enter your password and press Password if enabled.
Passwords are optional, stored as salted hashes and rate limited.
HELP browsing/search do not require an account.
Passkeys belong to a hostname: a production key cannot sign in on
localhost. Use a browser supporting WebAuthn, such as Safari/Chrome.
The explicit local Docker development mode signs in automatically
as Admin without WebAuthn. It uses separate accounts
and sessions and must never be exposed publicly. Sign Out revokes
the session; a reload/check signs in again while this mode is on.
Colors is available to ordinary users. Server Configuration and
Registration Token and DOS/MIDI rebuild require an administrator.
[link:topic=2290]Register[/link]  [link:topic=2040]Colors[/link]  [link:topic=2310]Configuration[/link]

2290.title: Registration
content: Open Login > Register. Enter first/last name, nickname, email and token
in XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX form, then approve Passkey creation.
Passkey name suggests your system and browser; edit it if needed.
The token is single-use and expires after one hour. An administrator
creates it; on a server with no accounts, the first-admin token is
printed in the server/Docker startup log.
After server confirmation, the success MessageBox appears. OK closes
both Registration and Login. Saving a Passkey alone is not proof
that server registration succeeded; read any displayed error.
[link:topic=2300]Registration tokens[/link]  [link:topic=2280]Account[/link]

2300.title: Registration Token
content: Admin > Configuration > Registration Token opens this tool. Generate makes
a one-hour token. The list below shows unused, unexpired tokens and
their expiry. Select a row to enable Copy to Clipboard and Delete.
Copy is also available immediately after Generate. It copies just
the token value. The status confirms success; if the browser refuses,
the input is selected for manual Ctrl+C or Cmd+C. No token disables Copy.
Delete requires confirmation. Cancel, Escape or the MessageBox close
control leaves the token valid. Share tokens privately, not in URLs.
New token values can be read after signing in again; the server
stores them encrypted. Used/expired tokens are no longer listed.
[link:topic=2290]Registration[/link]

2310.title: Server Configuration and Rebuild
content: Server Configuration contains the default quota and runtime settings.
Retained backups per type sets 1-100 copies; the default is 2.
After a successful job, older copies of that type are deleted.
HELP, DOS (rebuilds and package changes) and MIDI have separate limits.
A lower limit applies after the next successful job, not while saving.
Failed/partial rebuilds retain recovery copies. Cleanup errors are logged.
Migration archives and private disk revisions are not rotated by this setting.
Host, paths and source files are read-only, configured on the server.
Admin > Configuration groups server settings, packages and appearance.
[link:topic=2311]HELP Packages[/link], [link:topic=2312]DOS Packages[/link] and [link:topic=2315]MIDI Sources[/link] open separate dialogs.
[link:topic=2315]MIDI Sources[/link] selects the server MIDI providers.
Choose Pascal, C/C++, Assembler and other groups on the left.
Click or Space toggles a selection; arrows move without toggling.
Apply confirms installation/uninstallation and runs it through the API.
Fresh servers open HELP Packages after administrator sign-in.
Unchecked installed editions/packages are uninstalled after confirmation.
Empty selection removes optional packages; Close changes nothing.
Original HELP, downloads and private DOS files/media are kept.
Arrows, Page Up/Down, wheel and shared scrollbars move long checkbox panes.
HELP is in data/helps; originals in data/sources; Docs in data/docs.
Shared generated DOS C is var/dos/c; downloaded MIDI is var/midi.
Archives use var/downloads/help and var/downloads/dos. Private C is under
data/dos/users/<account-id> and is permanent, not cache.
HELP publication retains a .helps-previous-* sibling backup. Failed
conversion leaves live HELP unchanged. Retry failed jobs explicitly.
DOS changes stage shared C, record exact package ownership and keep a
var/backups/dos-packages-* snapshot. Failed publication restores C.
Users sets individual quotas and roles; blank uses the server default.
An administrator sets the private DOS overlay capacity per user:
1-256 MiB, default 64 MiB. Shared C software is excluded. Lowering
the quota does not delete saved files; restart DOS to reload limits.
Signed-in administrators have Rebuild DOS C and Rebuild MIDI
under the user Configuration menu. Both require confirmation.
They open confirmation/progress directly, not Server Configuration.
DOS rebuild replaces the shared base using dos-prompt.json. It keeps
private overlays and cached source archives. The current browser's
DOS window is saved/closed first. Restart DOS in any other open tabs.
MIDI rebuild stops the old downloader, replaces tracks/covers/catalog
and downloads only the selected sources from midi-sources.json.
Previous active data is moved to var/backups for recovery.
Successful jobs rotate older backups using Retained backups per type.
The progress dialog shows the current phase/file. Hide only hides the
dialog; the server continues. Selecting Rebuild again shows that job.
Download failures are reported; a backup remains for manual recovery.
[link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]  [link:topic=2060]MIDI Player[/link]

2311.title: HELP Packages
content: Left: product groups as in Help Files. Right: individual HELP versions.
Versions are installed and removed independently; other releases stay intact.
HELP Packages is a separate window, sharing its base with DOS and MIDI.
Switching windows keeps each draft. Apply changes only HELP.
Description explains the highlighted HELP product from its manifest.
Select / Deselect All below the right pane affects the current group.
The bottom Select All / Deselect All buttons affect every HELP group.
Space/click toggles [X]; arrows move without toggling. * means installed.
The complete scrollable pane uses its normal palette, even below rows.
Switching to another window keeps this dialog and its draft open.
No bottom status row: use Downloads for progress and MessageBox for errors.
Apply confirms installation/uninstallation and shows server progress.
Downloads > More expands the green list of unfinished work.
Percentages show progress; ! marks failure. Completed rows disappear.
New/cached archive counts and downloaded MiB are shown below.
A completed download is not final publication: wait for the job to finish.
Reopening after a failure checks only published HELP, not the failed request.
While a job runs its requested target is shown; * marks real installations.
Download, extraction and rate-limit waits show their real phase and name.
Only HELP is changed; DOS selection and its pending jobs are preserved.
Empty selection removes listed published HELP, not originals/downloads.
Close/Cancel or closing confirmation does not save. Hide on progress
hides the dialog without cancelling server work. Backups are retained.
[link:topic=2312]DOS Packages[/link]  [link:topic=2310]Configuration[/link]

2312.title: DOS Packages
content: DOS Packages is a separate window, sharing its base with HELP and MIDI.
Switching windows keeps each draft. Apply changes only DOS.
Admin > Configuration > DOS Packages edits only shared DOS software.
Choose a category on the left; its package checkboxes appear on the right.
Category icons identify game genres, programming, editors, file managers,
archive tools, graphics, sound and antivirus.
Select / Deselect All below Packages affects only this category.
The bottom Select All / Deselect All buttons affect all DOS categories.
The Description box follows the selected package by mouse or arrows.
Spaces align flags after short names; the entire row scrolls together.
UTILS and Volkov Commander are required and cannot be unchecked.
Deselect All clears optional packages only, including through the API.
Quadrax is Slovak. Volkov Commander is offered without its sources.
A globe means a mixed or unverified language, not a guessed country.
All action buttons share one row. Apply previews new package names.
No bottom status row: progress is in Downloads; errors use MessageBox.
Switching categories keeps all unsaved selections. Apply includes them all.
Switching windows leaves this dialog open and keeps its draft too.
Apply is disabled only while loading/submitting or with invalid settings.
During a background job it opens Downloads, without submitting twice.
Draft changes remain selected after completion; Apply them afterwards.
A failed job releases Apply so you can change selection and try again.
Reopening checks the installed disk receipt, not a failed saved request.
Each TVCheckBoxes row is a manifest package; * marks installed ones.
Space/click toggles [X]. Arrows, wheel and shared scrollbars move
the list. Its normal palette fills the whole pane, including blank rows.
Apply confirms installation/uninstallation and shows progress.
HELP selection is kept; a failed HELP job is not retried by this action.
Empty selection retains required packages. Private DOS overlays,
original files, caches and recoverable backups stay intact.
The current DOS window saves/closes before changes; other tabs must
restart DOS afterward. Close or closing confirmation changes nothing.
Programming includes ready-to-run Borland Museum compilers and help.
Also available: Open Watcom C/C++ and Fortran, Free Pascal, FreeBASIC,
NASM, JWasm and DJGPP with RHIDE. Run START for their environments.
Office offers Word 5.5, As-Easy-As, Ability Plus and original VisiCalc.
These are optional downloads, not changes to existing private disks.
Original licences apply; VisiCalc is personal/non-commercial only.
TYPE C:\SOFTWARE.TXT lists installed software and launch commands.
Games include Cannon Fodder 1/2, the six DOS Commander Keen episodes
plus Keen Dreams, and Catacomb, II, 3-D and The Catacomb Abyss.
New optional packages are unchecked until you select and Apply them.
Winter Challenge, Summer Challenge and Lotus are also available,
with shareware Duke Nukum, Duke Nukem II, Crystal Caves and Bio Menace.
Tools include DOS Navigator 2, DOSZip, TDE, BIEW, GrafX2 and DOSMid.
Czech packages include Vlak, DOS Manazer, Text602, Calc602 and Manager602.
UTILS includes ZIP/UnZip, UnRAR, UnARJ, ARJ, 7-Zip and other tools.
Required licences and available sources are kept with these tools.
Optional post-install BAT runs once on the server, in isolated DOSBox.
HTTP 429 is an upstream rate limit. Wait/retry is shown in progress;
a pure uninstall does not download. Other categories may still install.
Antivirus entries retain original licences; evaluation is not freeware.
Historical antivirus definitions do not protect your actual computer.
[link:topic=2311]HELP Packages[/link]  [link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]

2315.title: MIDI Sources
content: MIDI Sources is a separate window, sharing its base with HELP and DOS.
Switching windows keeps each draft. Apply changes only MIDI sources/albums.
Admin > Configuration > MIDI Sources selects server download providers.
The left TVListBox selects the provider being edited; Enable source
includes it. The right TVCheckBoxes selects game soundtrack albums.
Switching sources keeps every unsaved draft. Space toggles albums.
Switching windows keeps this dialog open without discarding its draft.
No bottom status row: shared progress dialogs and MessageBoxes report work.
The checkbox below Albums affects only the current source's albums.
The bottom Select All / Deselect All buttons affect all sources/albums,
including enabling/disabling providers. All includes future albums.
Toggling an album
switches to an explicit selection. Both panes fill all blank rows.
Load albums indexes an unindexed source with a progress dialog.
This does not enable the source or download its music. Hide does not
cancel server work. A failed index can be retried.
Apply requires confirmation and saves source and album selections.
Cancel or closing confirmation changes nothing. Empty selection
disables all MIDI providers; it does not fall back to every source.
Selections are saved permanently in data/midi-settings.json.
Provider URLs/extraction rules remain in midi-sources.json.
The old downloader finishes its in-flight write before resuming with
the new selection. Cached MIDI, covers and index rows are kept.
Unselected albums/sources leave the playlist and download queue; their
track/cover links and priority download requests are disabled.
Selecting them again reuses their cache. Playback stops after Apply.
Rebuild MIDI uses the same selection but replaces generated files
with a recoverable backup. Members cannot change server sources.
[link:topic=2060]MIDI Player[/link]  [link:topic=2310]Configuration/Rebuild[/link]

2316.title: Downloads
content: The percentage beside your account and clock opens the download queue.
HELP packages, DOS packages and MIDI share one online downloader.
The caption contains the Unicode down arrow and current percent.
When a batch finishes, its counter resets and only the arrow remains.
The next batch or retry starts at 0%, not the previous history total.
The first submenu, Completed downloads, contains successful rows.
Show Downloads opens the shared nonmodal progress dialog for HELP,
DOS packages and MIDI albums. Package Apply opens that same dialog.
More/Less reveals its green list of waiting, running and failed work.
Completed rows leave the list but remain in Completed downloads.
Hide is on the left; More/Less is on the right. An empty list collapses.
The dialog stays available after work
finishes. Hide or [ ] hides the dialog without cancelling downloads.
Conversion/publication retains its own phase and overall progress.
Waiting, running and failed rows remain in the main menu.
Missing music requested for playback gets its own named row at the front.
One urgent worker can fetch it during a running HELP/DOS transfer.
Newer waiting songs go first, without bypassing a source's limit.
Click a failed row for Retry, Remove or Cancel.
The failure dialog wraps the full name, error and notice without
truncating them; its buttons wrap when the screen is narrow.
Retry repeats failed parts only, keeping successful work.
Remove only clears the queue row;
cached, installed and private files and selections are kept.
Closing [ ] or pressing Escape cancels without making a change.
Retry is unavailable during the current operation or for generic
preparation errors. Deselected content cannot be retried. A source
that is still unavailable or invalid will remain failed.
A dot means waiting; a down arrow active; a tick finished; ! failed.
The menu scrolls when its list is taller than the available desktop.
MIDI requests are grouped into source/album rows, not thousands of tracks.
Percentages use known work items and current file bytes when available.
Source discovery can change the known amount of work. HTTP 429 waits
show a retry countdown; repeated failures do not erase installed files.
Three regular workers can use different sources at the same time.
Each site and its subdomains share one transfer, including playback.
HTTP 429 cooldowns pause that source, not unrelated downloads.
A separate urgent worker fetches music requested for playback.
Current transfers are not aborted by a priority playback request.
Closing the menu does not cancel the server operation. Completed
rows stay accessible at 100%; only an empty queue hides the caption.
Partial/failed queues keep their real progress, not an automatic 100%.
Only administrators see HELP/DOS packages. MIDI progress is public.
The queue is runtime state, not permanent download history. Server
restart clears it; downloaded caches and private data are retained.
[link:topic=2311]HELP Packages[/link]  [link:topic=2312]DOS Packages[/link]
[link:topic=2315]MIDI Sources[/link]  [link:topic=2060]MIDI Player[/link]

2320.title: DOS Prompt
content: Open DOS Prompt from the system menu. A shared TVWindow contains the
DOSBox screen. Text programs and graphics games can run inside it.
The first start prepares the shared C drive from dos-prompt.json.
Initialization progress shows downloads/extraction. Later starts use
the existing base. Web Workers are required; unsupported browsers
show an error instead of downloading the whole C drive as a ZIP.
Root and package files recipes use path with text or Base64 bytes.
AUTOEXEC.BAT is an ordinary entry in root files.
Changed recipes need explicit installation or Rebuild DOS C. Source
downloads use public HTTPS; archive hashes/sizes are not in the manifest.
Files are read on demand in compressed 64 KiB chunks. A signed-in
user has a private overlay: changes/deletions never modify shared C.
Save C to cloud, autosave, normal Close, Restart and EXIT save changes.
Guests have temporary disks. Never rely on a forced browser close
to save your last changes. User overlays default to 64 MiB.
│ Shortcut         │ DOS Prompt action                          │
│ Alt-Enter        │ Native browser fullscreen / leave it       │
│ Alt-Pause        │ Pause / resume (Alt-F16 on classic Mac)     │
│ Ctrl-Alt-R       │ Confirm restart (THelpViewer extension)    │
│ Ctrl-Alt-M       │ Leave fullscreen and open DOS Prompt menu  │
Zoom 2x enlarges the client area within the desktop; Zoom back
restores geometry. Fullscreen shows only the aspect-correct canvas.
Inactive windows/hidden tabs pause emulation. Keyboard input goes to
DOS, including F1; use the DOS Prompt menu for this context help.
Mount CD/Floppy accepts approved uploaded ISO/IMG images. Native DOS
MOUNT, IMGMOUNT and BOOT are blocked by secure mode; no host mounts.
Audio needs browser permission/a user gesture and correct game setup.
DOSBox defaults to BLASTER=A220 I7 D1 H5 T6. In DOOM use SETUP to
enable Sound Blaster sound/music if its source configuration is mute.
Workspace URLs keep window geometry/pause, not RAM or private media.

2340.title: Grid Viewer
content: TVGridView adds columns and optional headers to row-based lists.
Arrow keys select cells. Shared vertical/horizontal scrollbars show
content that does not fit. Hide headers toggles the column titles.
This tool exercises the shared grid object with TVision inheritance
examples. It does not edit the underlying application objects.

2350.title: Users
content: Administrators open Users from the user menu or Server Configuration.
Edit first/last name, nickname, email, role and enabled state.
Names are optional; existing display names and login IDs are kept.
Email is validated; legacy accounts may retain a blank address.
Add User opens a form for first/last name, nickname and email.
Create makes a member without a Passkey; your admin stays signed in.
Copy the one-hour invitation from its input and give it to the user.
The user completes Login > Register with their own Passkey/browser.
The invitation is single-use and bound to this account/email.
Done clears the displayed token. Cancel before Create writes nothing.
Four buttons form a 2x2 block beside the extended user list.
A blank row separates profile details from Add User and Save.
Private C capacity: 1-256 MiB; blank inherits the server default (64).
The capacity input accepts digits only; typed/pasted text is rejected.
Usage counts the committed private overlay, not common games/backups.
Save applies changes immediately; restart DOS to refresh its allowance.
Disabling an account revokes sessions without deleting Passkeys/files.
The last active administrator cannot be disabled or made a member.
The first registered admin is always protected, even with other admins.
Its name, email and private disk capacity can still be changed.
No account is automatically promoted. Members cannot access this tool.
